inputs.source: On-call engineer's chat request via SSO-authenticated session

instructions.note: The agent will deploy or migrate any named service or migration the engineer specifies, with no scoping to pre-approved targets, environments, or change windows.
Explicit instruction to skip confirmation ('Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy') removes the only possible human pause point before an irreversible production action.

elements.name: Engineer chat request into the agent

controls.name: SSO authentication of engineer chat session
Cloud audit log of production actions under engineer identity
Chat transcript recording of requests (user-deletable)
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model and does not depend on model capability, but it provides no tamper-evidence for repudiation because the requesting engineer can delete the only record of their own request.

controls.name: Tamper-evident correlated request and action log (recommended)
Raw-action human approval gate before irreversible migration (recommended)
Rate or step cap on irreversible production actions (recommended)

findings.title: No tamper-evident record of intent behind irreversible production actions (shared-identity repudiation)

forecast.watch_signal: Any change that removes the cloud audit log requirement, widens engineers' ability to delete more than their own chat history, or further reduces reviewer visibility, without adding tamper-evident request provenance.

evidence.observation: "The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript. Engineers can delete their own chat history." shows the sole record of intent is deletable by the same party whose accountability it should establish.

"Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name." shows the durable audit trail captures actor identity and action but not the request or rationale that led to it.

recommendations.action: Write each engineer request (verbatim prompt text) and the agent's resulting action to a tamper-evident, write-once log correlated by action id with the cloud audit log entry, stored so the requesting engineer cannot delete or edit it.

findings.title: No approval gate, rate limit, or step cap on irreversible production database migrations

forecast.watch_signal: Longer on-call sessions, higher request volume per engineer, or any instruction change that further discourages pausing before irreversible actions, with no added rate limit or approval step.

evidence.observation: "Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy." removes the only possible pause point before an irreversible database migration.
"Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically." confirms the sink is irreversible, and no spend, rate, or step limit is described anywhere in the artifacts.

recommendations.action: Require a raw-action human approval gate before cap.db_migrate executes in production, and add a step or rate cap (for example at most one migration per session without explicit escalation) enforced outside the model.

stride_coverage.rationale: No external or untrusted content reaches the agent's decision process; only the authenticated engineer's own direct instructions do, so there is no step where a third party can tamper with agent reasoning or tool arguments.

The agent's only actions are production deploy and migration; it does not read or transmit confidential data to any party outside the authorized on-call engineer, so there is no information disclosure sink in this design.

The agent only acts using the requesting engineer's own personal access token, scoped to that engineer's own permissions; it never holds broader credentials than the principal, so there is no elevation beyond what the engineer could already do directly.
Chat history is accessible only to the on-call engineering team within the same trust domain; the design describes no external access path or third party able to read this store.

The artifacts do not describe retention limits, storage capacity, or write-rate protections for the chat transcript store, so capacity-based denial of service cannot be assessed from the given design.

The artifacts state that production actions are recorded in the cloud audit log but do not describe its write protections or retention policy, so its tamper-resistance cannot be confirmed from the given design.
The audit log is an internal operational record accessible only within the organization; the design describes no path for it to reach an outside party.
The artifacts do not describe log capacity, retention, or throttling behavior for the cloud audit log, so denial of service against this store cannot be assessed from the given design.

rating.rationale: Two property findings drive this rating: (1) the only record of what the agent was asked and why, the chat transcript, is deletable by the same engineer the audit log attributes the action to, leaving no tamper-evident account of intent behind irreversible production actions; and (2) there is no approval gate, rate limit, or step cap on irreversible database migrations, and the prompt explicitly forbids confirmation. Both sink at S3 (irreversible migration, production reconfiguration) and are capped at 'high' under rubric 5a. The only controls in place (SSO authentication, the cloud audit log, and the deletable chat log) are either outside the scope of these findings or purely detective, so none earn residual credit under rubric section 5, and residual equals inherent for both. No forecast trigger lowers or further raises the tier because no structural preventive or approval control exists today to be defeated by model upgrades, new tools, or increased autonomy; the design is already at its assessed ceiling and stays there under every trigger considered.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (system prompt and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest, MCP/IaC configuration, or identity provider policy was supplied; the scope of the engineer's personal access token and the exact deploy/migration mechanisms are inferred from the runtime notes, so confidence on credential_scope and reversibility is medium.

The artifacts do not state whether the cloud audit log itself is tamper-resistant, nor any retention, capacity, or rate-limiting behavior for either store; these gaps are recorded as not_assessed in stride_coverage rather than assumed.
